design.d1: src/pages-modules/multiplayer/useGmRewindProducers.ts gains an exported pure buildGmRewindRequest(input): IPreviewGmCombatRewindInput | null, lifted verbatim out of onPreviewRewind. useGmRewindProducers keeps calling it, so its behaviour and the existing page-level pins are unchanged. The correction hook uses the SAME builder, which is how the correction request is byte-identical to the rewind request the GM is shown the blast radius for.
design.d2: src/pages-modules/multiplayer/useGmCorrectionProducers.ts (new): useGmCorrectionProducers({matchId, wireToken, mirrorEvents, preview?, commit?}). onPreviewHostGmCorrection builds the request, pins it in a ref and delegates to preview (default previewGmCombatRewind). setPrivateReason(reason) writes a ref only. onApproveHostGmCorrection calls commit (default commitGmCombatRewind) with the pinned request, spreading { reason } ONLY when the captured reason is non-empty after trim; with no request pinned it throws GmCombatRewindTransportError, mirroring useGmRewindProducers' confirm.
design.d3: The reason never reaches a store, a wire event, a projection or public state: it is held in a useRef inside the hook and appears in exactly one place, the commit call's argument object. It is not React state, not sessionStorage, not the preview request, and not the preview text.
design.d4: src/components/multiplayer/NetworkedGameSurface.gmCorrection.tsx (new): NetworkedHostGmControls MOVED out of NetworkedGameSurface.tsx (which measures ~382 effective lines against the oxlint max-lines warn threshold of 400, leaving ~18 lines of headroom - the same file-size reason the rewind controls were extracted), keeping all three existing test ids, gaining an optional onPrivateReasonChange?: (reason: string) => void and, when it is supplied, an uncontrolled text input labelled 'Private reason (GM only)' with data-testid networked-gm-private-reason. The control also renders the preview answer it gets back as one authored sentence (data-testid networked-gm-correction-preview-status) using the existing phrasing helpers, so the Preview button is not the defect-#15 shape of a control that calls the server and shows nothing.

risksForTheParent: PRIVACY, the unit's whole point: a private reason that leaks into the preview request, a store, a rendered string or a broadcast event would be a privacy defect shipped under a privacy review class. Mutant M3 exists to make that failure mode runnable rather than argued.

The reason does not reach the server on this head. Until the transport and route successor lands, POST /api/matches/[id]/rewind-commit still records REWIND_COMMIT_REASON. A reader of the UI could reasonably believe the typed reason was persisted. The hook's JSDoc and the receipt's nonClaims say so explicitly; the parent may want the input labelled or gated differently before merge - that is a product judgement, flagged not decided here.

Moving NetworkedHostGmControls into its own file is a diff-shape change on a component two existing suites assert on (NetworkedGameSurface.test.tsx and NetworkedGameSurface.rewind.test.tsx). It is justified by the ~18 lines of max-lines headroom measured on NetworkedGameSurface.tsx, but it is the largest single reviewable chunk in the diff.

Widening the two correction prop signatures touches src/pages/e2e/networked-command-proof.tsx's contract without editing that file. tsc --noEmit is the only thing standing between a wrong widening and a broken proof page, since no Playwright runs here.

NetworkedGmRewindControls and NetworkedHostGmControls now both drive the same underlying rewind request from the same surface. They are separate controls with separate buttons; nothing serialises them. Two concurrent GM clicks are the server's concern (correction-lease-held), not this unit's, but the parent should know the shape exists.
